plan.concept: RANSAC robustly estimates a model by finding a minimal sample of points that maximizes consensus among all data points, effectively ignoring outliers.
learningObjectives: The student will understand how RANSAC uses a minimal sample set (2 points for a line) to generate candidate models.
The student will be able to explain how the inlier threshold determines which data points support a candidate model.
The student will recognize how consensus voting allows RANSAC to ignore corrupting outlier points that would ruin standard least-squares fitting.
plan.keyInsight: Instead of trying to fit all points at once and getting dragged off-course by outliers, RANSAC finds the model that has the most 'agreement' among a subset of data points, letting the true structure vote down the noise.

interactions.label: Candidate Sample
interactions.effect: Cycles through different pairs of randomly selected points (highlighted in red) and draws the corresponding candidate line through them.
interactions.teaches: Shows how different pairs of points generate wildly different candidate models, some poor (incorporating outliers) and some excellent (the true line).

interactions.label: Inlier Threshold
interactions.effect: Visualizes a shaded envelope or tolerance band around the candidate line. Points falling inside this band turn blue (inliers); points outside remain white (outliers).
interactions.teaches: Demonstrates how the threshold parameter defines the tolerance for noise and directly determines the inlier count.

demo_steps.title: The Outlier Problem
demo_steps.narration: Look at the scatter plot containing several data points. Notice that while many points form a clear linear trend, there are a few isolated points on the right. Standard regression techniques would be dragged down by these outliers, yielding a skewed line that fits nothing well.
demo_steps.focus: The scatter of points, highlighting the visual contrast between the linear cluster and the isolated outliers.

demo_steps.title: A Bad Random Guess
demo_steps.narration: Change the candidate sample to see what happens when RANSAC randomly picks a sample containing an outlier. The resulting red line fits the two selected red points perfectly, but when we look at the consensus, almost no other points fall within our shaded threshold band.
demo_steps.focus: The red line tilted steeply toward the outliers, and the very low count of blue inlier points.

demo_steps.title: Adjusting the Tolerance
demo_steps.narration: Now try widening the inlier threshold. Notice how more points are captured as 'inliers' as the shaded region expands. If we make this threshold too wide, we risk classifying true outliers as inliers, which degrades the accuracy of our final fit.
demo_steps.focus: The widening shaded band around the line and the change in point colors.

demo_steps.title: Finding the Winning Consensus
demo_steps.narration: Switch the candidate sample to the optimal pair and lower the threshold back to a reasonable level. By picking two points from the main trend, the resulting line perfectly aligns with the cluster, capturing 9 inliers (blue circles) and leaving the noise points outside as outliers (white circles). This is the winning model!
demo_steps.focus: The optimal red line passing through the main cluster, with 9 blue inliers highlighted.

plan.reconstructionNotes: An interactive 2D scatter plot with x and y axes. Contains approximately 11 data points: 9 positioned roughly along a diagonal line with minor noise, and 2 outlier points far to the right. The user can cycle through different candidate lines. A red line is drawn through two highlighted red 'sample' points. A translucent colored envelope representing the 'inlier threshold' surrounds the line. Points inside this envelope are colored light blue (inliers); points outside are white with a black outline (outliers). An overlay text dynamically displays the inlier count (e.g., '9 inliers').
